title: taskkill shim: dated version history + design lessons
desc: T3 reference for taskkill-compat-shim-a11y-first-kill-routing: dated verification history, version bumps (v1.5-v2.0), and hard-won design lessons (parent-tree validation, symmetric protection)
steps: Verified 2026-05-03: callout window placement during wkappbot taskkill now validates monitor home via MonitorFromWindow(MONITOR_DEFAULTTONULL) in CalloutInputWindow.Ctor.cs SourceInitialized; orphan windows snap to primary monitor work-area+20,20 via SetWindowPos with SWP_NOACTIVATE. Resolves BUG-AUTO 2026-05-02T18:14:50.

v1.5 (2026-05-06): --force-all REMOVED. --force <pids> is the ONLY kill path. Default = classify-only + exit 1. PIDs not in --force list always survive. Verified via PowerShell: /IM exits 1 with full classification; --force 52600 kills exactly 52600 (76988 survives); --force-all returns exit 2 unknown flag.

v1.6 (2026-05-05): --force output now shows BOTH a KILLED block (--force list) AND a PRESERVED block (other matching PIDs in /IM scope, or wkappbot family if no /IM) with classification tags. Footer adds Killed: N / Preserved: M plus a hint to follow up on surviving zombies.
v1.7 (2026-05-06): taskkill classify and --force KILLED/PRESERVED per-PID lines now include image, parent PID/name, creation time as HH:mm:ss, reason, and cmdline truncated to 100 chars.

FOCUS-STEAL false-positive during a11y-kill: the single-pid IsPidDead guard is insufficient because kill-by-pattern kills MULTIPLE pids and Windows transiently reassigns foreground during the taskkill cascade. Fix: FocusStealSentinel suppression must be TRANSACTION-SCOPED and MULTI-PID-AWARE -- snapshot ALL candidate victim PIDs into a HashSet<int> before the kill starts. Principle: foreground loss caused by our own destructive kill is never focus-steal.

v1.9 (2026-05-28): PARENT-PROCESS-TREE VALIDATION. taskkill was killing unrelated Chrome processes (different parent tree). Fix: 8-step GetParentProcessId ancestor walk before kill decision -- only allow killing descendants of the closest AI process (bash/pwsh/claude/code.exe) in the chain; others PROTECTED. Reason: taskkill from user-IDE should not kill user personal Chrome, only wkappbot Chrome in the same AI family tree.

v2.0 (2026-06-02): RULE 0 -- live AI-session ancestor protection. GetLiveAiSessionAncestorPids() scans running claude/codex/gemini PIDs, builds a HashSet including each AI CLI PID + 16-deep parent chain. ClassifyOne checks this set as rule 0 (highest priority, before empty-cmdline ZOMBIE check) -- any PID in the set is PROTECTED, preventing AI from self-terminating its own parent console. Only AI CLI processes count as session roots. Commit aa1d00583.

DESIGN LESSON -- asymmetric protection (2026-06-02): the v1.9 ancestor-chain walk was one-sided -- it protected USER processes from AI but never protected AI hosting terminals from being killed by ANOTHER AI invocation. Lesson: protection rules must be SYMMETRIC. Fix pattern: build a GLOBAL set (GetLiveAiSessionAncestorPids) up-front so any PID hosting an AI session is PROTECTED before any per-process classification runs -- this is rule 0, before any identity check.
author: claude
